text:
Jaroslav Chmelar got the call back from Hartford on Nov. 2 (the New York Post's Mollie Walker reported Taylor Raddysh went the other way), and The Hockey News ran a piece that week on him being critical of his own early-season play. Five days later he scored in Seattle, beating Joey Daccord for his first goal of the season in a 4-3 win.

That goal is the whole scoring line so far: one point in 10 games at about 8 minutes a night. The 6-foot-5, 238-pound winger is used for weight more than touch, with 19 hits, and the closest match to his style in our numbers is Edmonton's Trent Frederic. He can move, too: his top skating speed, 22.9 mph, sits in the 91st percentile by NHL EDGE.

The worry is what happens when he's out there. The Rangers get 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, nearly 12 points worse than the team does without him. A fifth-round pick fighting for a spot needs to tilt the ice. We'd watch whether that share climbs with steady minutes; if it doesn't, the shuttle to Hartford keeps running.
headline: Chmelar's second chance starts with a goal
